applied.problem: 'Is how the size of an AC voltage or current is defined' is too absolute: peak and peak-to-peak are also used (scope readings, insulation); the source calls it the general idea. 'Whatever the shape' overstates a true-rms meter, which has bandwidth and crest-factor limits.

325² ÷ 52.9 is 1997 W, not exactly 2000 W (2000 comes from the unrounded peak), so it needs 'about'; 0.637 of the peak is the sine's half-cycle average only; and readings may be marked peak-to-peak as well as peak.
